description: Immutable per-stage anomaly counts for a completed processing run. Keyed on the SAPPHIRE stage ordinal (stage_num), not the TD ordinal -- anomalies are gated to sapphire's (ttr, rampdown_start] window.
sql: SELECT CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS fleet_name, CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS pad_name, CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS processing_run_id, CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS algorithm_version, CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS source_signature, CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS name, CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE PRECISION) AS stage_num, CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS stage_start_ts, CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS stage_end_ts, CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS source_rows, CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE PRECISION) AS total_anomaly_lines, CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE PRECISION) AS pressure_surge_lines, CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE PRECISION) AS pump_rate_drop_lines, CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE PRECISION) AS mid_stage_shutdown_lines, CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE PRECISION) AS sweep_lines, CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS created_at FROM datastore:merged_fleet_stream_customer_full_v2 WHERE 1 = 0

gate_start_ts.description: Sapphire ttr. Anomalies are evaluated in (gate_start_ts, gate_end_ts]; NULL means the stage was not gated and contributes no anomaly rows.

gate_end_ts.description: Sapphire rampdown_start -- the first sustained leave from design rate that never recovers.

gate_status.description: ok | no_ttr | no_rampdown | no_telemetry. Why a stage produced no anomalies, without needing to join back to the sapphire summary.
